lead.hed: USNI: Navy wants a standoff aerial torpedo for carrier aircraft
lead.insight: USNI News, Friday: the Navy is looking to develop a next-generation standoff torpedo that can be carried by carrier-based aircraft and drones. Naval Air Systems Command released a request for information Tuesday on the Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo. Defense News, Tuesday: the Navy is exploring a new glide torpedo or a glide kit on an existing weapon, with industry replies due Sept. 29. The service asked for a compact round no heavier than 268 pounds and a prototype within 18 months after an agreement award. An RFI is a market survey, not a production buy.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class William Bennett IV · DVIDS 9675020 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · Aviation Ordnanceman 3rd Class Jeffery Price loads a Mark 54 lightweight torpedo onto a P-8A Poseidon at Kadena Air Base, Japan. Date taken May 7, 2026. Caption must say May file photo, not today’s RFI.
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Navy DVIDS still of a torpedo load on a P-8A. Same-subject class as the Silent Anvil air-launched torpedo survey — not the recycled Hormuz Roosevelt still, not an F-15, not a brand tile.

political.hed: USNI: Hormuz tanker transits rose more than 30 percent last week
political.insight: USNI News, Friday evening: transits through the Strait of Hormuz rose more than 30 percent last week, led mostly by tankers and gas carriers. Lloyd’s List Intelligence counted 114 transits between Aug. 17 and Sunday, compared with the Aug. 10–16 week. The count is still below pre-war levels and is likely to move as more dark tankers are identified. The item is a weekly traffic tally, not a Navy declaration that the strait is open.

political.hed: USNI: Abraham Lincoln entered the Malacca Strait on Friday
political.insight: USNI’s Western Pacific Pulse, Friday: USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) entered the north end of the Malacca Strait on Friday, according to automatic identification system data. The Pulse is a weekly ship-movement summary. The Navy did not publish a next port in that item.

political.hed: Navy accepts the last Expeditionary Sea Base, named for a Marine
political.insight: Navy press release, Wednesday: the service accepted delivery of USNS Hector A. Cafferata Jr. (ESB 8) from General Dynamics NASSCO in San Diego on Aug. 25, after integrated sea trials this summer. The ship honors Marine Pfc. Hector A. Cafferata Jr., Medal of Honor at Chosin Reservoir. It is the sixth and final ESB. The Navy has not named an operating area.

tech.hed: CISA adds ownCloud, Linux kernel, and JFrog holes to the exploited list
tech.insight: CISA on Thursday added three flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: CVE-2023-49105 in ownCloud, CVE-2026-53362 in the Linux kernel, and CVE-2026-66384 in JFrog Artifactory. Binding Operational Directive 26-04 tells federal civilian agencies to prioritize listed high-risk holes on publicly exposed assets. CISA encourages other operators to treat the catalog the same way; the directive itself binds federal agencies.

tech.hed: OpenAI letter: a limited window to strengthen cyber defense
tech.insight: OpenAI published an open letter Thursday calling for collective action on cyber defense as AI-enabled attacks get cheaper. The posted roster includes Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, AMD, and more than a hundred other firms. The letter asks governments to fund defense for hospitals and water plants. It is a joint appeal, not a statute.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Kafka’s court still maps how scapegoats are made
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: Daniel H. Burns reads The Trial as a picture of justice that starts blindfolded, grows wings as activism, and ends as the hunt. He argues online antisemitism now skips the legal costume and sells bloodlust as entertainment. The essay is a reading of Kafka, not a crime blotter.

watch.hed: WATCH: Air Force F-15 ceiling is $131 billion, not a jet on signing
watch.insight: Defense News, Friday: the Air Force awarded Boeing a sole-source F-15 Eagle Crest contract with a $131.23 billion ceiling through 2037. The Aug. 24 notice obligated $343,740 in fiscal 2026 research money at award. Saturday PM keeps the ceiling on Watch.
